tips.label: Exercise daily
tips.text: Go for a brisk walk, run, or do housework to release endorphins and reduce tension. [1, 2]

tips.label: Prioritize sleep
tips.text: Aim for 7 to 9 hours of nightly sleep to allow your body to recover from daily demands. [1, 2]

tips.label: Eat a balanced diet
tips.text: Focus on fruits, vegetables, and whole grains while avoiding excess caffeine, alcohol, and refined sugar. [1, 2]

tips.label: Engage your senses
tips.text: Step outside, listen to calming music, hold a warm blanket, or use deep breathing and meditation apps like Calm or Mindfulness Coach. [1, 2, 3]

tips.label: Practice box breathing
tips.text: Inhale for 4 seconds, hold for 4 seconds, exhale for 4 seconds, and hold for 4 seconds to lower your heart rate. [1]

tips.label: Reframe negative thoughts
tips.text: Challenge catastrophic thinking or perfectionism, and replace harsh self-talk with realistic expectations.

tips.label: Take control of what you can
tips.text: Break large problems down into small, manageable tasks or set a 20-minute timer to focus on a single action.

tips.label: Set boundaries
tips.text: Learn to say "no" to non-essential commitments and protect personal time ("me time") away from work.

tips.label: Connect with others
tips.text: Talk through your troubles with a trusted friend, family member, or colleague to build a support network.

tips.label: Limit media intake
tips.text: Cut back on checking the news or scrolling social media when it triggers anxiety. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8]

If stress feels overwhelming, persists for a long time, or interferes with your daily responsibilities, consult a primary care physician, a counselor, or a mental health provider for guidance. [1, 2, 3]

tips.label: Stick to a schedule
tips.text: Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day, including on weekends. [1]

tips.label: Wind down
tips.text: Spend 30 to 60 minutes before bed doing calming activities like reading, stretching, or taking a warm bath. [1, 2]

tips.label: Turn off screens
tips.text: Avoid phones, tablets, computers, and TVs at least 30 to 60 minutes before bedtime to prevent blue light from blocking melatonin. [1, 2]

tips.label: The 20-minute rule
tips.text: If you cannot fall asleep after 20 minutes, get out of bed and move to another room to do a quiet activity until you feel sleepy. [1]

tips.label: Keep it cool and dark
tips.text: Set your bedroom temperature to a cool setting (around 65°F–68°F) and use blackout curtains, an eye mask, or a sleep mask.

tips.label: Block out noise
tips.text: Use earplugs or a white noise machine if your sleeping space is noisy.

tips.label: Reserve the bed
tips.text: Use your bed only for sleep and intimacy; avoid working or watching TV in bed. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

tips.label: Limit stimulants and alcohol
tips.text: Avoid caffeine and nicotine in the afternoon and evening. Do not use alcohol close to bedtime, as it disrupts deep sleep cycles.

tips.label: Watch heavy meals
tips.text: Avoid large or greasy meals right before bed, though a light snack is fine if you are hungry.

tips.label: Exercise regularly
tips.text: Get physical activity during the day, but finish vigorous workouts a few hours before bedtime.

tips.label: Manage daytime naps
tips.text: Keep naps short (under 20–30 minutes) and avoid napping late in the afternoon. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
